title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Zone Transfer Concurrency Architecture
design_summary: The existing DoQ adapter architecture already supports concurrent zone transfer requests. DoqClient.QueryAsync opens a new stream per call without blocking other calls, enabling parallel IXFR/AXFR requests. DoqServer.HandleQueryStreamAsync dispatches each stream independently as a Task, allowing interleaved responses. QUIC's stream multiplexing provides head-of-line blocking freedom. This slice adds verification tests confirming zone transfer concurrency.
data_and_state_considerations: No new adapter state. All concurrency is handled by the existing stream-per-query architecture and QUIC transport.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The adapter does not define zone-transfer-specific semantics beyond standard query/response.
Concurrency is bounded by MaxInboundBidirectionalStreams and QUIC flow control.
risks: Large zone transfers may exhaust stream flow control windows; this is managed by the QUIC transport.
The adapter treats AXFR/IXFR as regular DNS queries; no special streaming protocol is implemented.

supplemental_sections.heading: Existing Architecture
supplemental_sections.content: Slice 0002 established the client-initiated bidirectional stream-per-query model. Slice 0003 established server-side concurrent stream handling with resource limits. Both are sufficient for zone transfer concurrency without architectural changes.
